decisions.executionNote: Begin left-tube approach with a gradual elbow-up lift and downward wrist rotation; keep right arm at origin.
Continue forward over the left tube, rotating the open gripper to a downward approach aligned across its body.
Finish aligning the left gripper with the tube and descend slowly to just above grasp height; visual centering remains approximate.
Use wrist feedback to center the tube between the fingers, correct its in-plane angle, and lower one centimeter before closing.
Close around the left tube, then make a small vertical test lift and inspect retention in RGB.
Tube appears retained between the fingers. Lift clear of the table while beginning a controlled rotation toward upright.
Transport the retained tube toward the rack’s left slot, rotating gradually upright while keeping its tip clear.
Complete upright rotation and approach above the leftmost large front-row slot, keeping the gripper closed.
Begin slow insertion approach, moving slightly right to center the tube over the left slot; check tip alignment before descending further.
Lower the upright left tube toward insertion depth with no lateral sweep; inspect its seating before release.
Tube appears to have contacted the slot edge. Relieve the contact by lifting, then shift slightly forward to center its tip.
Lower slowly at the corrected alignment, retaining the tube and watching for rim contact or further slipping.
Make a small centering adjustment, release the tube over the slot, and withdraw slightly to inspect whether it settles upright.
Withdraw the open left gripper to clear the rack and inspect the released tube; its seating is uncertain.
Clear the left side of the rack fully to assess the released tube without gripper occlusion.
The released tube is leaning. Re-approach its exposed upper body with the open left gripper to correct its seating.
Adjust the open gripper toward the exposed tube cap using wrist feedback, without closing against the rack.
Center on the exposed cap, grasp cautiously, and lift slightly to recover the leaning tube for realignment.
Lift the recovered tube clear of the rack while retaining the cap grasp, then inspect its orientation before correcting upright.
Rotate the cap-held tube toward upright, raising the wrist to compensate for the fingers swinging downward and keep the tube clear.
Replan after the continuity guard with smaller rotation and lift increments, retaining the recovered tube.
Continue slowly orienting the cap-held tube toward vertical while maintaining clearance above the rack.
Bring the cap-held tube upright and shift its tip above the left large slot, lifting slightly for rim clearance.
The recovered tube is nearly vertical. Shift its visible tip right and forward over the left front-row hole, maintaining a small clearance.
Center the visible tip over the left front hole and lower the cap-held tube slowly into the opening.
Lower the vertical cap-held tube another three centimeters at the apparent slot center, monitoring retention and rim contact.
Visible tip appears near the front rim rather than inside. Lift a little and shift forward and slightly left to center the opening.
Descend slowly along the aligned tube axis to seat the tube in the left opening; keep the cap grasp closed.
The tube remains in front of the rack. Lift clear and move further forward over the opening before attempting another descent.
Lower at the corrected forward alignment, watching for the tip to disappear into the left rack opening.
Continue a controlled short descent now that the tube tip is at the slot plane; check seating before releasing.
Release at the apparent seated depth and lift the open gripper clear to verify the tube’s upright stability.
Clear the rack with the open left gripper and let the released tube settle; its placement is not yet confirmed.
Withdraw the left arm while the displaced tube settles; begin a gradual elbow-up approach to the nearer right-side tube.
Continue the right arm’s open downward approach to the nearer tube; park the left arm away from the rack.
Center the nearer right tube in the wrist view while finishing the downward orientation and approaching grasp height.
Align the right gripper across the tube body and advance slightly toward its cap before closing.
Close around the nearer right tube and make a small test lift to verify retention visually.
The right tube is retained. Lift it clear before rotating upright and transporting it toward the rack’s right opening.
Rotate the right tube toward upright in small continuous increments while moving inward toward the right rack slot.
Continue the upright rotation with the right tube held securely, approaching above the rightmost large opening.
Finish orienting the held tube upright above the rack’s right side and approach insertion height without releasing.
Descend with the upright right tube, correcting slightly inward over the right large slot while retaining the grasp.
Continue the slow vertical insertion with the right tube held closed, checking for displacement at the rim.
The tube appears to contact the rim. Relieve it with a small lift, then correct slightly outward and toward the front of the right opening.
Try the corrected right-slot alignment with a slow three-centimeter descent, keeping the tube retained until seating is visible.
Release the right tube at the apparent slot depth and withdraw gently, allowing it to settle before judging the insertion.
The released right tube appears upright in the opening. Withdraw clear of it and begin repositioning for the remaining right-side tube.
Reposition the open right gripper above the remaining right tube, turning downward while staying clear of the inserted tube.
Advance above the far right tube and continue turning the open gripper into a downward grasp orientation.
Finish the downward wrist orientation and approach over the far right tube, keeping the fingers open for visual centering.
